title: MITI Report 2018
publisher: Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), Malaysia
methodology: Annual ministry report; p. 71 groups animation, games and interactive media, film/TV VFX, and new media/platforms as Digital Content & Creative Technology Industry.
assessment: Authoritative but unusable for games employment: reports 11,590 jobs created for the combined sector in 2018, not a games-only workforce stock.
next_step: Do not series-code. Seek a DOSM establishment/occupation table that explicitly isolates game development.

title: Southeast Asia Game Industry Report 2021
methodology: Three-phase regional study. Phase 1 was a 67-question survey of 151 gaming-industry players in six countries; Malaysia was 61% of respondents. Includes benchmarking and synthesis.
assessment: Games-specific but a voluntary regional survey, not a Malaysian employment census. Contains company-size bands and response distributions, no national stock.
next_step: Use only to document survey scope; do not extrapolate to a workforce count. Earlier 2015 and 2016 editions were identified but no official file recovered in this pass.

title: Southeast Asia Digital Content Industry Talent Report 2022
methodology: Regional online survey/interviews across six countries; sample mixes animation and game-development participants (reported 56% animation and 44% game development).
assessment: Not games-only and not a national census; useful only as an exclusion record.

title: Southeast Asia Game Development Industry Talent Economics Report 2024
methodology: Two regional online surveys across Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam: 295 individual respondents and 48 studios. Focuses on pay, experience, qualifications, studio growth and talent requirements.
assessment: Games-specific but survey evidence, not a Malaysia population count. No annual workforce-stock series.
next_step: Do not series-code; retain for qualitative methodology context only.

title: Advancing Malaysia's Digital Creative Industry Towards AI Nation 2030
methodology: Press release; no employment methodology or sector allocation published.
assessment: Authoritative government communication but reports 'over 11,000 high-value jobs' for the whole digital creative industry and says jobs were created to date. Not games-only and not stock.
next_step: Do not series-code. Request underlying MDEC administrative series only if it supplies games-only annual headcount and definitions.

title: Cultural and Creative Satellite Account 2024
methodology: National cultural-and-creative satellite account; publishes aggregate employment for the cultural and creative industry.
assessment: Official national employment source, but its published headline is 763.1 thousand across the cultural and creative industry, not games. It cannot isolate game development from the headline material reviewed.
next_step: Inspect detailed satellite-account tables only if a games-specific activity/product cell is documented.
